position: Righting the Ship: Review Retroactively; Implement Repair
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the next President direct State to freeze ongoing treaty and international agreement negotiations pending an alignment review, stand down enforcement of treaties the Senate has not ratified, and review (with the Attorney General and White House Counsel) which 'agreements' are in substance treaties and suspend compliance until they are sent to the Senate. It also recommends moving to withdraw from treaties that have been before the Senate for 20 years or more, updating the transmittal where a stale treaty is still worth ratifying.
remaining: A freeze or alignment review of ongoing treaty and agreement negotiations.
A review identifying agreements that are in substance treaties, with compliance suspended pending Senate transmittal.
Withdrawal of treaties that have been pending before the Senate for 20 years or more.
Publication of the findings of the Executive Order 14199 treaty review.

status_summary: No government-wide freeze of treaty negotiations, no stand-down on unratified treaties and no review sending treaty-like agreements to the Senate was found. The closest actions are withdrawals from existing instruments: Executive Order 14162 (signed 2025-01-20) directed notice of withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, which the UN depositary records as taking effect for the United States on 2026-01-27, and Executive Order 14199 (signed 2025-02-04) ordered a 180-day review of all treaties and conventions to which the US is a party. A 2026-01-07 memorandum (91 FR 2281) then directed withdrawal from 66 organizations and named one convention, the UNFCCC; the depositary records the US notice as effected 2026-02-27, effective 2027-02-27. These concern instruments already in force, not the Senate-pending or unratified categories the Mandate describes.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14162 directed immediate written notice of US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and from other commitments made under the UNFCCC.

Executive Order 14199 directed the Secretary of State to review, within 180 days, all international organizations and all conventions and treaties to which the US is a party and to recommend whether to withdraw.

A presidential memorandum directed agencies to withdraw from 35 non-UN organizations and 31 UN entities, naming the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change; it does not mention the Senate or unratified treaties.
The US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement took effect, per the UN depositary notification of 2025-01-27 recording receipt of the US notice that day.
The UN depositary recorded the US withdrawal notice under the UNFCCC as effected on this date, with withdrawal effective 2027-02-27.

title: Freeze treaty talks, stop enforcing unratified treaties, send treaty-like deals to Senate
uncertainties: Searches for a government-wide freeze of treaty negotiations, a stand-down on unratified treaties, a review of agreements that are in substance treaties, and any withdrawal of treaties pending before the Senate found no matching action; this is an absence finding. The Paris Agreement was concluded without Senate advice and consent, so its withdrawal is parallel to, not the same as, the Mandate's unratified-treaty category. The findings of the Executive Order 14199 treaty review have not been published beyond the January 2026 memorandum, which says review of further findings remains ongoing; the State Department site could not be reached to check for a separate publication. Inference: the Paris withdrawal is operative, so a reader could argue for in_progress; the review keeps proposed because the operative step concerns an instrument already in force rather than the freeze, stand-down or Senate-transmittal steps the text asks for.
